title: What If Your City Sank 10 Inches Every Year? Jakarta Is

scenes.text: What if a city of ten million people sank every year? Jakarta is doing it right now.
Parts of northern Jakarta sink about 25 centimeters a year, close to ten inches.
The cause is underground. People drill wells for water, and as pumps drain the ground, the land above drops.
Roughly 40 percent of the city now sits below sea level, so floods keep coming.
Some experts estimate a third of Jakarta could be underwater by 2050.
So Indonesia passed a law in 2022 to move its capital 2,000 kilometers away to Borneo, and name it Nusantara.
